finish.text: The fight for equality for Black Americans in the United States traces back to a couple of hundred years ago. One individual who made a large impact was W.E.B. Du Bois.

instruction.text: Read the text and answer the following questions.

atoms.text: William Edward Burghardt “W. E. B.” Du Bois was a Massachusetts born historian, sociologist, philosopher and great political leader in the late 19th century and early 20th century. Du Bois studied at Harvard University and the University of Berlin and received his doctorate in 1895 from Harvard University. This made him the first African American to earn a PhD at Harvard University. These were only a few achievements which influenced his later life, where he was an important actor in the early 20th century civil right’s movement.
atoms.sound: William Edward Burghardt “W. E. B” Du Boys was a Massachusetts born historian, sociologist, philosopher and great political leader in the late 19th century and early 20th century. Du Boys studied at Harvard University and the University of Berlin, and received his doctorate in 1895 from Harvard University. This made him the first African American to earn a PhD at Harvard University. These were only a few achievements which influenced his later life where he was an important actor in the early 20th century civil right’s movement.

atoms.text: Du Bois is known for having challenged Booker T. Washington’s stances on civil rights. Washington argued that Black Americans would gain acceptance and economic stability in society by proving themselves through both skill and labour. Du Bois saw this approach as problematic, for he believed that such an approach would only keep Black Americans in a disadvantageous position. At the beginning of the 20th century, the dispute between Washington and Du Bois polarised African American leaders into two wings - Washington’s supporters and Washington’s critics.

stance – a specific way of thinking or feeling.
disadvantageous - lacking an advantage; being in an inconvenient position.
dispute - a form of verbal fight
hint.label: Glossary

atoms.text: Armed with an impressive academic career and determined stance, W.E.B. Du Bois became one of the founders of the National Association for the Advancement of Coloured People (NAACP) in 1909. Du Bois became the editor of the organisation’s monthly magazine, The Crisis. He strived to raise awareness of the widespread practice of lynching, and he pushed for nationwide legislation that would outlaw the unjustified killings at the time.
